name: 163. MCP log deletion requires dashboard auth (#7769) (mcp-log-delete-auth)
description: Management-plane regression for #7769 using the default harness profile with dashboard auth disabled or unconfigured. A caller with no credential must be refused by DELETE /api/mcp-logs before body parsing or storage deletion. Under the OSS setup lock that refusal is the lock's 401, so the delete rows strip the X-Bifrost-Setup-Token header the harness injects: a request carrying the token is authenticated and is allowed to delete. The session-status precondition fails loudly when this folder is run against an auth-enabled profile. The valid-body probe uses a fresh GUID sentinel rather than an existing log ID, so even an unfixed gateway cannot delete real records; the handler Go tests independently assert zero storage calls and preserve authenticated deletion. Cookies, inherited auth, and redirect following are disabled. No authentication configuration is changed and no provider calls are made; openai is only a harness filter label. Run the whole folder in order with FEATURE=mcp-log-delete-auth and PARALLEL=0.
